purpose: Ramipril is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of having a heart attack or stroke. It is also used to help protect the heart and kidneys in people who have had a heart attack or who have heart failure. Doctors sometimes prescribe it to help protect the kidneys in people with diabetes.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to tighten and narrow, which raises your blood pressure. Ramipril blocks the enzyme that makes this chemical, so your blood vessels can relax and open up. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a safer level.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a dry, persistent cough that does not go away — this happens in some people and is the main reason patients switch medications. You might also feel dizzy, especially when you stand up quickly, or feel unusually tired. Some people notice mild headaches or an upset stomach when they first start taking it.
warnings: Do not take ramipril if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Rarely, it can cause a dangerous allergic reaction called angioedema — if your face, lips, tongue, or throat suddenly swell up, stop taking it and call emergency services right away. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, are taking potassium supplements, or are taking other blood pressure medicines, as ramipril can raise potassium levels in your blood to unsafe levels.
typical_dosing: Ramipril is usually taken once a day, often starting at a low dose of 2.5 mg. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over several weeks up to 10 mg per day depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled and how you feel. You can take it with or without food, and it is best to take it at the same time each day.
